name: lud
description: LU decomposition (lud): in-place non-pivoting (Doolittle) factorization of a 2048x2048 float matrix.

output_parser.comment: Each line is '<index>\t<value>'; compare column 2 (factored matrix cell) by index, row-major over N*N=4194304 cells.

tolerance.comment: Non-pivoting LU of this 2048x2048 matrix is ill-conditioned (cond~1.3e14); factor entries span 0..~6.6e4 (mean abs 26.6) and the sequential k-recurrence amplifies float32 rounding in the high-magnitude late rows. The intended phase-1 port is the STRAIGHTFORWARD data-parallel scheme (one thread per j, same increasing-k float accumulation as the serial), which reproduces the golden's accumulation order and matches bit-closely under --fmad=false; rtol/atol 1e-2 absorbs only minor benign float-order wiggle in the perimeter/column updates while flagging logic/indexing bugs, which corrupt the well-conditioned bulk and the L/U triangular layout. CAVEAT: a BLOCKED port (or any port that reassociates the k-accumulation) drifts far beyond this tolerance in the ill-conditioned tail and would be (correctly, for phase 1) rejected by an elementwise comparison; blocking is a phase-2 concern. Golden L,U reconstruct A with max relative residual 3.1e-3 (independent float64 check), confirming it is a valid factorization.

build.comment: Correctness build disables FMA contraction to match the CPU serial bit-closely; perf build uses defaults (FMA on) for realistic timing.
